newsitem.title: USA: Christian Coalition head asks for gambling panel.
newsitem.headline: Christian Coalition head asks for gambling panel.

text.p: Ralph Reed, executive director of the Christian Coalition, Tuesday called upon President Clinton to name the final members of a panel to study the impact of gambling on society.

The commission has become politically sensitive for Clinton after it was revealed that at least 10 members of the gambling industry attended coffees at the White House that were designed to court contributors to Clinton's 1996 campaign.

Clinton last year signed legislation creating a nine-member National Gambling Impact Study Commission. Although the House and Senate each designated three members of the panel, but the president has yet to name his choices.
"The American people deserve a serious, objective examination of the impact that gambling has on society, particularly the poor and downtrodden," Reed wrote in a letter to Clinton.

"We cannot afford further delays," said Reed, who voiced hope that Clinton's appointments "will send a clear message to the American people that campaign contributions have had no influence on the composition of this commission."
The gambling industry gave a total of some $5 million in political contributions to Democrats and Republicans during 1995 and 1996.
